subtitle: Lesson 42 · The chapter's capstone

eyebrow: The starting point: a real T-SQL procedure
caption: A realistic everyday T-SQL pattern — let's translate it decision by decision.

code:
-- @CustomerId INT  ->  p_customer_id IN NUMBER
-- DECLARE @OrderCount INT  ->  moved into ONE
-- DECLARE/IS section before BEGIN
CREATE OR REPLACE PROCEDURE get_customer_order_summary (
    p_customer_id IN NUMBER
) IS
    v_order_count NUMBER;
BEGIN
caption: No @ sigil; every local variable declared up front, not scattered.
PRINT becomes DBMS_OUTPUT.PUT_LINE; END IF is always required, every time.

eyebrow: Decision 4: the bare SELECT needs a REF CURSOR
code:
CREATE OR REPLACE PROCEDURE get_customer_order_summary (
    p_customer_id IN  NUMBER,
    p_orders      OUT SYS_REFCURSOR
) IS
...
OPEN p_orders FOR
  SELECT order_id, order_date, total_amount
  FROM orders WHERE customer_id = p_customer_id;
caption: The biggest structural change — T-SQL's free result-set return has no PL/SQL equivalent.

eyebrow: Plus an EXCEPTION section, added defensively
caption: The original had no TRY...CATCH, but a real PL/SQL translation should add one.
